measure_name: Project-financed climate and disaster risk assessment
definition: A project-financed climate and disaster risk assessment systematically evaluates hazards, exposure, vulnerability or potential impacts in order to inform a project activity, investment, design or operational requirement. Counts only when the project finances, commissions, carries out or explicitly requires a substantive assessment from an implementing agency, operator, consultant, contractor or bidder. The assessment may cover a site, route, asset, system, sector or investment program and may inform subsequent siting, design or operational measures, which should be classified separately. Bank appraisal-stage climate screening, CDRS, Paris Alignment analysis, climate co-benefits calculations, CCDR findings and general PAD descriptions of climate vulnerability do not count. An assessment completed outside the project does not count unless the project finances its preparation, update or substantive application as a project activity. The World Bank's screening of this project is excluded, but a screening or assessment that the project itself finances of its own or named sites, routes or investments counts. A law, rule or system requiring assessments of future investments in general is climate_governance, not this.
note: Deliberately excludes generic “climate screening” language because it is heavily contaminated by Bank appraisal processes. Positive classification requires a project activity or requirement, not evidence that the Bank assessed the project. v4 (2026-10-20): Dev's revision; measures are defined by the intervention, the asset map gives the asset.
